project.title: Hex counter with a working seven-segment display
project.question: How does a four-bit counter drive a seven-segment digit?
project.notes:
A clock drives a four-bit counter. An explicit HEX7 decoder maps its digit and decimal point onto the eight-bit SEG7 segment bus.

Expected: The display starts at 0, advances through 1–9, A, b, C, d, E, F, then wraps to 0. Each visible update follows the rising clock by 20 ns (counter plus decoder delay). Decimal point stays off.

Try: Inspect different simulation times. Set both decoder and display active levels to low, or switch the decoder to BCD to blank counts 10–15.
assumptions: The display is a passive digital indicator. It does not model LED electrical loading or brightness.
Bit 0=a, 1=b, 2=c, 3=d, 4=e, 5=f, 6=g, 7=decimal point. Words are MSB first.
The displayed state comes from the current project revision and preserved simulation events at the selected time.

annotations.text: Run, then inspect a time: the display follows the actual segment bus.
HEX7 and SEG7 active levels must match. Bit 7 is the decimal point.
